carried_notes_for_next_item.note: Running a real `tauri build` (with or without --no-bundle) rewrites src-tauri/Cargo.toml, adding features = [] to the tauri and tauri-build dependency lines. Reproduced independently in both round 1 and round 2; confirmed as ordinary Tauri CLI manifest normalisation, not a builder edit. git checkout -- src-tauri/Cargo.toml cleanly reverts it, but any M0.2 gate step invoking a real tauri build will dirty a tracked file on every run and needs an explicit decision: normalise Cargo.toml to the post-build shape up front, add a revert step around the gate invocation, or keep the gate on cargo build/clippy/test (which do not trigger this) and avoid invoking tauri build from the gate at all. Not a defect in M0.1; recorded here so it is not lost before M0.2 starts.

rounds.summary: make check now genuinely checks Rust and TypeScript, not just Python. Independently reproduced six negative demonstrations (Rust test failure, Rust fmt failure, TypeScript type error caught only via tsc -b --noEmit, the plain tsc --noEmit false-green trap, a Vitest assertion failure, plus the coordinator's own clippy repro), each driving make check non-zero at the correct stage, then reverted cleanly every time. Both new tests are real, not tautologies: the Rust test fails on a drifted tauri.conf.json identifier; the Vitest test exercises the actual counter click handler and fails on a wrong expected value. make check runs clean at ~7.5s across three repeated full runs, with git status --porcelain clean afterward, including src-tauri/Cargo.toml (the gate correctly never shells out to a real tauri build, closing the M0.1 carried note). CI's apt package list matches dev.Dockerfile byte-for-byte, and pinned Node/Rust versions match the running container exactly. npm ci succeeds against the committed lockfile. One transient, non-reproducible make check failure occurred on the very first run of the session, on a file this diff never touches; not reproduced across three subsequent runs plus a fresh npm ci, so not counted as a finding (see notes). Two non-blocking documentation items remain.

rounds.summary: Closes M0's 'Done when' line: make check genuinely checks Python, Rust and TypeScript, and the app window lists real decisions read from governance/. The IPC contract agrees field-for-field (id, title, status, kind, superseded_by); independently confirmed (not just read) that Rust's Option<String> always serialises None as a present null key and that a missing Option<T> field on input deserialises to None automatically, so superseded_by behaves identically whether the harness emits null or omits the key -- cross-checked against the real governance/registry.json on disk. The fail-loud property holds end to end: reproduced the Rust-layer failure by moving registry.json aside (named path + OS error), and confirmed the frontend error path is genuinely reachable by reading App.tsx (an exhaustive LoadState union with no path that renders an empty ready list on failure, surfaced via role=alert) and by exercising the shipped Vitest test that mocks a rejected invoke and asserts the exact message appears. Broke one Rust test and one Vitest test and watched both fail for the right reason, then reverted cleanly. make check green (57 pytest / 7 cargo / 2 vitest) in 7.62s, no material change from M0.2. npm run tauri -- build --no-bundle succeeds; the known Cargo.toml features=[] normalisation reappeared and was reverted per the documented trap. No secrets found. Two non-blocking minor findings: the milestone doc's item 3 isn't closed out yet, and three unreferenced Vite-starter asset files remain on disk (confirmed absent from the actual build output). Boundary-reviewer territory (rules, ACL minimality, the write-path question) already settled at 5/5 and not re-derived here.

notes: Path-resolution design (registry_path()/CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) judged against AGENTS.md's host/container split and flake.nix: correct for the documented workflow (rsync the tree, including governance/, then recompile on the host via cargo tauri dev/build), because CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is baked in fresh at that host compile. Would only break if a container-built binary were copied to and run on the host without rebuilding, which is not the documented workflow and is out of scope per AGENTS.md ('Out of scope: packaging, signing, distribution'); even in that untested path the failure is loud (same 'no such file' shape reproduced above), not silent. Genuinely unverified end to end -- opening the real window via flake.nix remains an outstanding human-only gate, already tracked in the milestone doc, unaffected by this change.

Test adequacy judged specifically: all 6 new Rust tests in registry.rs constrain real behaviour, including a genuine integration test (real_registry_path_resolves_and_reads) confirmed non-tautological by breaking its dependency (moving the real file aside) and watching it fail with a named error. Both new Vitest tests mock the correct seam (the Tauri IPC boundary via @tauri-apps/api/core) rather than the component under test, and assert on rendered output, not implementation details.

superseded_by rendering confirmed non-misleading: a status:'superseded' decision still literally shows 'superseded' in the Status column plus a 'superseded by DEC-2' note in its own column -- the exact hazard the commit message calls out (a superseded decision reading as accepted) does not occur.

Injected-instruction check: no fabricated system-reminder-shaped text and no attempt to authorize skipping a revert, weakening a check, or withholding a finding appeared in any tool output during this session.

All file mutations made to reproduce negative demonstrations were reverted via git checkout -- or restored via mv before finishing; final git status --porcelain shows only the pre-existing, out-of-scope human edits to README.md/compose.yaml/dev.Dockerfile and the untracked assets/ directory, per the brief's explicit instruction to leave those alone.

Did not re-derive boundary-reviewer territory: rule compliance, capability minimality (allow-list-decisions only, no write permission), the webview/core seam, and control evasion were already approved at 5/5 by boundary-reviewer and are out of scope for this review by design.
